question: What causal mechanisms remain credible for Attempt 3 after inspecting the champion, real-tender corpus, and evaluated experiment history?
findings:
The champion retrieves the raw line plus at most one canonical alternate, collapses raw/canonical hits to the best rank within each modality, RRF-fuses dense and BM25, and gives only the untouched raw line to DeepSeek for final selection. In the reconstructed 130-row review set, 48 are ball-valve requests, 45 contain threaded/inch cues, 43 contain third-party brand/model cues, 33 concern filters/water treatment, and 20 contain work-action wording. The LD CSV has no IVR, VALTEC, cartridge/ЭФГ, or water-treatment terms. Of the 20 action rows, some explicitly name a valve or filter product, so action wording alone is not a safe abstention signal.

The local, nearby retrieval space is now substantially saturated: endpoint/inch expansion, vendor-token suppression, manufacturer-fact enrichment, quantity-boundary repair, and variant-aware fusion all had neutral or unsafe end-to-end results. The latter two are especially important because code confirms their premises, but their evaluated changes still increased wrong-NOT_FOUND or failed public safety. Evidence supports investigating request granularity and catalog-scope uncertainty rather than another lexical or fusion refinement.
decision_impact: The central uncertainty is whether unresolved tender value is mostly recoverable product evidence obscured by mixed service/product line items, or honest catalog-scope uncertainty for requests outside LD’s sellable taxonomy. The next experiment should discriminate those explanations while preserving raw retrieval and avoiding a forced MATCHED/NOT_FOUND decision. There is insufficient evidence for another nearby branded-model, endpoint/inch, canonicalization, parser, or query-variant-fusion refinement.
unresolved: The review pool is unresolved, so category prevalence is not proof of end-to-end uplift. Lexical absence from the catalog is supporting evidence rather than proof of product absence; any scope mechanism needs affirmative taxonomy/category evidence and a fail-open path. The supplied review-pool gzip remains unreadable locally, but its 130 members are exactly reconstructable from the intact full corpus minus the 90 labels and 33 provisional cases.

evidence_patterns.pattern: Semantics-preserving retrieval changes have a narrow success boundary; semantic completion and alternate-ranking changes have not safely improved end-to-end outcomes.
supporting_experiments: Legacy cycles 6, 9, and 17 rejected flanged, standard-bore, and actuation semantic expansions.
Attempt 1 query_evidence_preservation improved public known-positive hit rate but raised hidden wrong-NOT_FOUND by 0.08.
Attempt 2 query_variant_evidence_fusion raised public wrong-NOT_FOUND by 0.04.
evidence_patterns.interpretation: The code confirms that canonical variants are currently collapsed before RRF, and that a quantity-boundary defect exists. But both a repair of that defect and preservation of variant provenance have already been scientifically evaluated without safe end-to-end value. These are not credible nearby repeats absent new causal evidence.

evidence_patterns.pattern: Genericizing third-party nomenclature or importing external product facts repeatedly harms abstention safety.
supporting_experiments: Attempt 1 threaded/inch alias expansion: hidden wrong-NOT_FOUND +0.04.
Attempt 3 trusted manufacturer/model enrichment: hidden wrong-NOT_FOUND +0.08.
Review corpus: 43 branded/model-like rows; catalog lexical scan: no IVR or VALTEC tokens.
evidence_patterns.interpretation: Branded nomenclature is a real lexical mismatch, but the repeated failure signature indicates that source-product facts and generic wording do not establish an appropriate LD equivalent. This family is locally saturated.

evidence_patterns.pattern: Selection-adjacent candidate manipulation is high risk, but catalog scope is a distinct product problem not addressed by retrieval.
supporting_experiments: Legacy cycles 1–2, 5, 7, 8, and 16 found gating, compatibility prompting, index enrichment, fallback substitution, or diversification neutral or harmful.
Review corpus: 33 filter/water-treatment rows; 13 contain cartridge/ЭФГ/sorbent/water-treatment cues without a valve-family cue.
Catalog lexical scan: no cartridge/ЭФГ or water-treatment terms.
evidence_patterns.interpretation: Broad filtering or selection rules should not be retried. A narrowly affirmative catalog-scope mechanism is causally different if it reports uncertainty rather than selecting a substitute or asserting catalog absence from weak evidence.

evidence_patterns.pattern: Tender lines mix procurement work with product nouns, making line-item granularity a plausible upstream bottleneck.
supporting_experiments: Review corpus: 20 rows contain installation, removal, disassembly, repair, or maintenance actions.
Five action rows also name a valve-family product; examples include installation/removal of ball valves and a line containing a butterfly-valve product.
Current canonicalization extracts a textual clause but has no explicit work-versus-product decomposition.
evidence_patterns.interpretation: An action-word NOT_FOUND rule would be unsafe, but separating an explicit purchasable product phrase from surrounding work language could distinguish recoverable product requests from service-only requests. This is materially different from supplier-token suppression.

candidate_directions.causal_mechanism: Use affirmative, catalog-taxonomy-backed evidence that a requested category is outside LD’s sellable product scope to return an explicit uncertain/no-catalog-evidence outcome, while retaining ordinary retrieval for ambiguous or product-bearing lines. Do not infer absence from a single unmatched token and do not substitute an unrelated LD item.
candidate_directions.competing_explanation: The apparent noncoverage may be catalog synonymy or a retrieval/index representation failure; routing could hide a valid LD product or create wrong NOT_FOUND behavior.
candidate_directions.falsifier: A blinded manual review of a stratified non-benchmark sample finds viable LD products for a material share of rows meeting the proposed combined cues, or regression evaluation increases wrong-NOT_FOUND.
candidate_directions.information_gain: High. It directly tests whether a meaningful part of real-tender difficulty is catalog scope rather than retrieval, while aligning with the product goal’s preference for honest uncertainty.

candidate_directions.causal_mechanism: Extract a bounded purchasable-product span from mixed work/service nomenclature and use it only as an additive retrieval representation; retain the complete raw line and leave final compatibility selection unchanged. Service-only spans should not manufacture a product query.
candidate_directions.competing_explanation: Mixed work wording may be useful context, and the apparent product phrase may be too underspecified to improve retrieval; decomposition could repeat unsafe genericization under another name.
candidate_directions.falsifier: On a stratified real-tender sample containing both action and product cues, extracted product spans do not improve family-consistent candidate presence/rank over raw retrieval, or public/hidden guardrails regress.
candidate_directions.information_gain: High. It separates recoverable product mentions embedded in work descriptions from genuinely service-only lines without relying on the already-rejected branded-model transformations.

candidate_directions.causal_mechanism: Represent insufficient technical evidence separately from a confident product match and expose a useful candidate set or an explicit uncertainty reason when multiple candidates remain plausible, instead of making the final interface binary by default.
candidate_directions.competing_explanation: The current reranker can already select multiple candidates, so the bottleneck may be candidate quality rather than result semantics; extra states may add complexity without changing user utility.
candidate_directions.falsifier: A sampled review workflow shows that the proposed uncertainty state does not improve the ability to distinguish unsupported, underspecified, and viable multi-candidate requests, or it encourages unsupported matches/abstentions under regression gates.
candidate_directions.information_gain: Moderate-to-high. It tests whether measured pipeline failures partly arise from a binary decision contract that cannot faithfully express the product goal, rather than from another retrieval-rank adjustment.
